sentences.nl: En deze aflevering bevat woorden, die te maken hebben met het thema: ‘reizen’.
sentences.en: And this episode contains words related to the theme: 'travel'.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And this episode contains words, that to do have with the theme: 'travel'.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "En deze aflevering bevat" translates to "And this episode contains." The verb "bevat" is in the present tense, matching the subject "deze aflevering."  
• "die te maken hebben met" translates to "that have to do with." It's a common phrase used to indicate relevance or relation to a topic.  
• "het thema: 'reizen'" means "the theme: 'travel'." The colon is used to introduce the theme explicitly.  

Examples:  
• "De film bevat scènes, die te maken hebben met oorlog." (The movie contains scenes that have to do with war.)  
• "Dit boek bevat informatie, die te maken heeft met geschiedenis." (This book contains information that has to do with history.)  

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "En dit artikel bespreekt onderwerpen, die te maken hebben met gezondheid." (And this article discusses topics that have to do with health.)  

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• (No cultural note applicable.)

sentences.nl: Dit is Lars.
sentences.en: This is Lars.

sentences.nl: Lars reist vandaag van Zweden naar Nederland.
sentences.en: Lars is traveling from Sweden to the Netherlands today.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Lars travels today from Sweden to Netherlands.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence follows the Subject-Verb-Time-Place (SVTPO) order, typical in Dutch.  
• "Reist" is the present tense of "reizen" (to travel).  
• "Vandaag" (today) is an adverb of time and usually placed after the verb.  
• Prepositions "van" (from) and "naar" (to) indicate direction or movement.

   - Hij reist morgen van Amsterdam naar Parijs. (He travels tomorrow from Amsterdam to Paris.)
   - Ze gaat elke week van huis naar kantoor. (She goes from home to the office every week.)
   - We vliegen overmorgen van Duitsland naar Italië. (We fly from Germany to Italy the day after tomorrow.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Anna loopt elke dag van het station naar haar werk. (Anna walks every day from the station to her work.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Sweden and the Netherlands are both part of the Schengen Area, allowing for easy travel between the countries.

sentences.nl: Hij reist niet met de auto.
sentences.en: He does not travel by car.

sentences.nl: Hij heeft geen auto.
sentences.en: He doesn't have a car.

sentences.nl: Hij reist met het vliegtuig.
sentences.en: He travels by plane.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• He travels with the airplane.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Hij reist" is in the present tense, indicating an action happening now or regularly.  
• "Met" is a preposition meaning "with." It indicates the means of transportation here.  
• "Het vliegtuig" means "the airplane." "Het" is the definite article for neuter nouns.

• Example 1: "Zij reist met de trein." (She travels by train.)  
• Example 2: "Ik ga met de auto." (I go by car.)  
• Example 3: "We gaan met de bus." (We go by bus.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Wij reizen met de boot." (We travel by boat.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Air travel is a common way to travel between countries in Europe, and many people in the Netherlands use flights for both business and leisure trips.

sentences.nl: Om 12 uur landt hij op Schiphol.
sentences.en: He lands at Schiphol at 12 o'clock.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• At 12 o'clock lands he at Schiphol.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses inversion, which is common in Dutch when a time, place, or other element starts the sentence. Here, "Om 12 uur" (At 12 o'clock) is at the beginning, so the subject "hij" (he) follows the verb "landt" (lands).  
• "Om" is a preposition used with specific times.  
• "Schiphol" is the name of the main airport in the Netherlands, and no article is needed before it.

Examples:  
– Om 8 uur begint de vergadering. (At 8 o'clock the meeting begins.)  
– Op zondag speelt hij voetbal. (On Sunday he plays soccer.)  
– In de zomer gaan we naar het strand. (In the summer we go to the beach.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Om 3 uur vertrekt de trein naar Amsterdam. (At 3 o'clock the train departs for Amsterdam.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Schiphol is one of Europe's busiest airports and is located near Amsterdam. It's often just referred to by its name without "luchthaven" (airport) because it's so well known.

sentences.nl: Dat is het vliegveld van Amsterdam.
sentences.en: That is the airport of Amsterdam.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• That is the airport of Amsterdam.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Dat is" is a simple construction meaning "that is." It is often used for identification or pointing out something.  
• "Het vliegveld" is a noun phrase meaning "the airport," with "het" as the definite article for neuter nouns.  
• "Van Amsterdam" indicates possession or association, similar to "of Amsterdam" in English. "Van" is a preposition used to indicate origin or belonging.

• Examples:  
  - Dit is het huis van mijn ouders. (This is the house of my parents.)  
  - Dat is de fiets van Peter. (That is the bike of Peter.)  
  - Dit is het boek van de leraar. (This is the book of the teacher.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Dat is het museum van de stad. (That is the museum of the city.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Schiphol Airport is the main international airport of the Netherlands, located near Amsterdam. It is one of the busiest airports in Europe and a hub for international travel.

sentences.nl: Hij gaat van het vliegveld met de trein naar Drenthe.
sentences.en: He goes from the airport by train to Drenthe.

sentences.nl: Lars heeft nog geen kaartje voor de trein.
sentences.en: Lars does not have a ticket for the train yet.

sentences.nl: Hij staat bij de automaat.
sentences.en: He is standing by the vending machine.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• He stands by the vending machine.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Hij staat" uses the verb "staan" (to stand) in the present tense.  
• "Bij" is a preposition meaning "by" or "near."  
• "De automaat" is a noun phrase meaning "the vending machine." The definite article "de" is used for common gender nouns in Dutch.

• Example 1: Zij zit bij de tafel. (She sits by the table.)  
• Example 2: Wij wachten bij de ingang. (We wait by the entrance.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Zij staat bij het raam. (She stands by the window.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, vending machines ("automaten") are commonly used for snacks and drinks, as well as for items like train tickets in stations.

sentences.nl: Hij begrijpt het niet.
sentences.en: He doesn't understand it.

sentences.nl: Eh…
sentences.en: Uh...

sentences.nl: Heb je hulp nodig? zegt de man achter hem.
sentences.en: Do you need help? says the man behind him.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Have you help needed? says the man behind him.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses a question structure: "Heb je hulp nodig?" which literally means "Have you help needed?" This is a common way to ask if someone needs help in Dutch.  
• "Zegt de man achter hem" means "says the man behind him." The word order in Dutch places the verb "zegt" (says) before the subject "de man" (the man), which is typical in main clauses following a question or introductory phrase.  
• "achter" means "behind" and is used as a preposition here.

Extra examples:  
– "Heb je tijd over?" (Do you have time to spare?)  
– "Zegt de vrouw naast haar" (says the woman next to her)  

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Heb je een pen?" vraagt de vrouw naast haar. (Do you have a pen? asks the woman next to her.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, it's common for people to offer help or ask if help is needed in public settings, reflecting a sense of community and willingness to assist others.

sentences.nl: Eh ja, ik moet naar Drenthe.
sentences.en: Oh yes, I need to go to Drenthe.

sentences.nl: Ik wil een kaartje voor de trein.
sentences.en: I want a ticket for the train.

sentences.nl: Ik weet niet welk kaartje.
sentences.en: I don't know which ticket.

sentences.nl: Voor het openbaar vervoer in Nederland,, heb je een ‘OV-chipkaart’ nodig.
sentences.en: For public transport in the Netherlands, you need an 'OV-chipkaart'.

sentences.nl: Met die kaart betaal je in de trein,, de metro, de tram en de bus.
sentences.en: With that card, you pay in the train, the metro, the tram, and the bus.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• With that card pay you in the train, the metro, the tram, and the bus.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Met die kaart" (With that card) indicates the means by which something is done, using the preposition "met" (with).  
• "Betaal je" (pay you) is in the present tense and uses an inverted word order typical for questions and certain phrases following an adverbial clause.  
• "In de trein, de metro, de tram en de bus" (in the train, the metro, the tram, and the bus) lists modes of public transport, using the preposition "in" to indicate location.

• Extra phrases:  
  - "Met die pen schrijf ik de brief." (With that pen, I write the letter.)  
  - "Op die dag ga je naar het strand." (On that day, you go to the beach.)  
  - "In de ochtend drink ik koffie." (In the morning, I drink coffee.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Met deze sleutel open je de deur." (With this key, you open the door.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, the OV-chipkaart is commonly used for public transportation, allowing seamless travel across multiple transit types like trains, trams, buses, and metros. This card has largely replaced paper tickets.

sentences.nl: Lars heeft nog geen OV-chipkaart.
sentences.en: Lars does not have a public transport chip card yet.

sentences.nl: Eh… hoe werkt dat? — Eerst koop je een anonieme OV-chipkaart.
sentences.en: Uh... how does that work? — First, you buy an anonymous OV-chipkaart.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Eh… how works that? — First buy you an anonymous OV-chipcard.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Hoe werkt dat?" is a question structure where the verb "werkt" (works) comes before the subject "dat" (that), which is typical in Dutch questions.  
• "Eerst koop je" follows the word order of time-manner-place, with "eerst" (first) indicating time and "koop je" (you buy) as the main action.  
• "Anonieme OV-chipkaart" is a noun phrase where "anonieme" (anonymous) is an adjective modifying the noun "OV-chipkaart" (public transport chip card).

Extra Examples:  
• "Hoe gaat het met jou?" (How is it going with you?) - Similar question structure.  
• "Dan eet je een appel." (Then you eat an apple.) - Similar time-manner order.  
• "Hij heeft een nieuw boek." (He has a new book.) - Similar adjective-noun structure.

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Daarna lees je een boek. (Then you read a book.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The "OV-chipkaart" is a common method of payment for public transport in the Netherlands, used on trains, buses, trams, and metros. An anonymous card can be purchased without registering personal information, offering more privacy.

sentences.nl: Anoniem? — Ja, op een anonieme OV-chipkaart, staat geen foto en geen naam.
sentences.en: Anonymous? — Yes, on an anonymous OV-chipkaart, there is no photo and no name.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Anonymous? — Yes, on an anonymous public transport chip card, stands no photo and no name.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Anoniem" is an adjective meaning "anonymous." In Dutch, adjectives can precede nouns directly.  
• "OV-chipkaart" is a compound noun where "OV" stands for "openbaar vervoer" (public transport) and "chipkaart" means "chip card."  
• The phrase "staat geen foto en geen naam" uses the verb "staat" (stands/is) to indicate that something is absent or not present, which is a common usage in Dutch.  

Examples:  
- "Op de tafel staat geen boek." (On the table, there is no book.)  
- "Op mijn bureau staat geen computer." (On my desk, there is no computer.)  

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Op een lege fles staat geen etiket. (On an empty bottle, there is no label.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The OV-chipkaart is a contactless smart card system used for all public transport in the Netherlands. The anonymous version allows travelers to use public transport without their personal information being linked to the card.

sentences.nl: Deze automaat verkoopt anonieme OV-chipkaarten.
sentences.en: This machine sells anonymous OV-chip cards.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• This machine sells anonymous OV-chipcards.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Deze" is a demonstrative pronoun meaning "this." It's used for de-words, like "automaat."  
• "Verkoopt" is the third person singular present tense form of "verkopen" (to sell). Dutch present tense is used for actions happening now.  
• "Anonieme" is an adjective meaning "anonymous," describing "OV-chipkaarten." In Dutch, adjectives take an -e ending when they precede a noun.  
• "OV-chipkaarten" refers to public transport smart cards used in the Netherlands. "OV" stands for "Openbaar Vervoer" (public transport).

Examples:  
• Deze winkel verkoopt boeken. (This store sells books.)  
• Hij koopt een anoniem ticket. (He buys an anonymous ticket.)  
• De automaat is kapot. (The machine is broken.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Deze machine accepteert alleen munten. (This machine only accepts coins.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The OV-chipkaart is a contactless smart card system used for all public transport in the Netherlands, making travel convenient across trains, buses, trams, and metros. An "anonieme OV-chipkaart" is a non-personalized version that doesn't require personal registration.

sentences.nl: OK.
En dan? — Daarna moet je het saldo opwaarderen.
sentences.en: And then? — After that, you must top up the balance.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And then? — After that must you the balance top-up.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "En dan?" is a common phrase meaning "And then?" often used to ask what comes next.  
• "Daarna" is an adverb meaning "after that," indicating a sequence of actions.  
• "Moet je het saldo opwaarderen" follows the Dutch word order where the modal verb "moet" (must) is conjugated and placed before the subject "je" (you), followed by the object "het saldo" (the balance) and the main verb "opwaarderen" (to top up) in its infinitive form.  
• Example 1: "Daarna moet je de trein nemen." (After that, you must take the train.)  
• Example 2: "Daarna gaan we naar huis." (After that, we go home.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Eerst eet je het ontbijt en daarna moet je naar school gaan. (First, you eat breakfast and then you must go to school.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, public transportation often requires topping up a travel card balance, which is referred to as "opwaarderen."

sentences.nl: Saldo opwaarderen? — Jazeker.
sentences.en: Top up balance? — Certainly.

sentences.nl: Dan zet je bijvoorbeeld 50 of 100 euro tegoed, op de kaart.
sentences.en: Then you can, for example, load 50 or 100 euros credit onto the card.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Then put you for example 50 or 100 euros credit on the card.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Dan zet je" uses "zet" (put) in the present tense, indicating a habitual action or instruction.  
• "Bijvoorbeeld" means "for example," often used to introduce an example or illustration.  
• "Tegoed" refers to credit or balance, often used with prepaid cards or accounts.  
• Word order: The sentence shows a typical Dutch structure where time elements like "dan" (then) are placed at the beginning.

Extra phrases:  
• "Dan ga je naar de winkel." (Then you go to the store.)  
• "Zet het boek op de plank." (Put the book on the shelf.)  
• "Je krijgt bijvoorbeeld korting." (You get, for example, a discount.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Dan koop je bijvoorbeeld een cadeau voor je vriend." (Then you buy, for example, a gift for your friend.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Prepaid cards are commonly used in the Netherlands for public transport and various services, allowing people to load a specific amount of money onto a card for future use.

sentences.nl: Dat kan met een creditcard.
sentences.en: You can do that with a credit card.

sentences.nl: En dan kan ik reizen met die kaart? — Ja, maar bij elke reis moet je inchecken.
sentences.en: And then I can travel with that card? — Yes, but you have to check in for each trip.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And then can I travel with that card? — Yes, but at every trip must you check in.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "En dan kan ik reizen met die kaart?" - This is a question using inversion, where the verb "kan" (can) comes before the subject "ik" (I).  
• "bij elke reis moet je inchecken" - This uses "moet" (must) as a modal verb, which is followed by the base form of the verb "inchecken" (to check in). "Elke" means "every," indicating a routine or repeated action.  
• Example: "Kan ik hier parkeren?" (Can I park here?)  
• Example: "Bij elke maaltijd eet ik groenten." (With every meal, I eat vegetables.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "En dan kan ik met die kaart betalen?" (And then can I pay with that card?)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, public transport often requires checking in and out with an OV-chipkaart, which is a contactless smart card used for travel on trains, buses, trams, and metros. Not checking in or out properly may result in a fine.

sentences.nl: En uitchecken.
sentences.en: And check out.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And check out.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "En" is a conjunction meaning "and." It's often used to connect two related actions or ideas.  
• "Uitchecken" is a separable verb meaning "to check out," often used in the context of leaving a hotel or returning a borrowed item. In this sentence, it's used in its infinitive form.  
• Example phrases:  
  - "En inschrijven." (And register.)  
  - "Ik moet nog uitchecken." (I still need to check out.)  
  - "Hij wil uitchecken en vertrekken." (He wants to check out and leave.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "En inpakken." (And pack.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, hotel check-out times are typically around 11:00 a.m. to noon. It's advisable to confirm this with your hotel to avoid any extra charges.

sentences.nl: Het bedrag van de reis gaat van je saldo af.
sentences.en: The cost of the trip will be deducted from your balance.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• The amount of the trip goes from your balance off.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Het bedrag" means "the amount." "Van de reis" translates to "of the trip," showing possession.  
• The phrase "gaat van je saldo af" uses "gaat" (goes) with a separable verb "afgaan," meaning "to be deducted." In Dutch, the preposition "af" is separated and placed at the end of the sentence.  
• Example phrases:  
  - "De prijs van het boek gaat van mijn rekening af." (The price of the book is deducted from my account.)  
  - "Het geld gaat van zijn budget af." (The money is deducted from his budget.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Het abonnementsgeld gaat automatisch van je rekening af. (The subscription fee is automatically deducted from your account.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, public transport often uses a card system where travel costs are deducted directly from your balance, similar to how this sentence describes a cost being deducted.

sentences.nl: Oh, nou… dat is niet makkelijk.
sentences.en: Oh, well... that is not easy.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Oh, well... that is not easy.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Oh, nou..." is an informal expression often used to show hesitation or to introduce a response.  
• "Dat is niet makkelijk" is a simple sentence structure with "dat" (that) as the subject, "is" (is) as the linking verb, and "niet makkelijk" (not easy) as the predicate.  
• Example 1: "Nou, dat klinkt interessant." (Well, that sounds interesting.)  
• Example 2: "Oh, dat is niet wat ik verwachtte." (Oh, that is not what I expected.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Oh, nou… dat is nogal verrassend." (Oh, well… that is rather surprising.)

sentences.nl: Nee, bij mijn eerste keer in Nederland was het ook niet makkelijk.
sentences.en: No, during my first time in the Netherlands, it was not easy either.

sentences.nl: Maar als je het weet… dan is het niet moeilijk meer.
sentences.en: But if you know it... then it's not difficult anymore.

sentences.nl: Ik ga ook naar Drenthe.
sentences.en: I am also going to Drenthe.

sentences.nl: Ga jij eerst met de trein naar Zwolle? — Eh… ja.
sentences.en: Are you going to Zwolle by train first? — Uh… yes.

sentences.nl: Dan kunnen we samen reizen.
sentences.en: Then we can travel together.

sentences.nl: Ik leer je inchecken en uitchecken.
sentences.en: I teach you how to check in and check out.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• I teach you to check in and check out.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ik leer je" means "I teach you," where "leer" is the present tense form of "leren" (to teach/learn) and "je" is the informal second-person singular pronoun.  
• "Inchecken" and "uitchecken" are separable verbs in Dutch, meaning "to check in" and "to check out" respectively. These verbs often combine with prefixes like "in-" (in) and "uit-" (out).  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Ik leer je autorijden." (I teach you to drive a car.)  
  - "Hij leert haar koken." (He teaches her to cook.)  
  - "We moeten inchecken voor de vlucht." (We need to check in for the flight.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Ik leer je zwemmen in het diepe water." (I teach you to swim in the deep water.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, it is common for people to check in and out using public transportation cards called "OV-chipkaart." This is an essential part of daily commuting for many Dutch people.

sentences.nl: ‘Dat is heel aardig’, zegt Lars.
sentences.en: "That is very kind," says Lars.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• "Dat is heel aardig", zegt Lars.  
  ("That is very kind", says Lars.)

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Dat is heel aardig": "Dat" is a demonstrative pronoun meaning "that". "Is" is the present tense of "zijn" (to be). "Heel" is an adverb meaning "very", modifying "aardig" (kind).  
• "Zegt Lars": "Zegt" is the third person singular present tense of "zeggen" (to say). The subject "Lars" comes after the verb in this quotation structure.  
• Extra examples:  
  - "Dat is heel mooi." (That is very beautiful.)  
  - "Dat is heel duur." (That is very expensive.)  
  - "Zegt de leraar." (Says the teacher.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Dat is heel interessant", zegt Anna. (That is very interesting, says Anna.)

sentences.nl: Hoe heet jij? — Ik ben Soliman.
sentences.en: What is your name? — I am Soliman.

sentences.nl: Ik kom uit Egypte.
sentences.en: I come from Egypt.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• I come from Egypt.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ik kom uit Egypte" uses the present tense of the verb "komen" (to come) to indicate origin or nationality.  
• "Uit" is a preposition meaning "from," used to describe origin or source.  
• The sentence structure is Subject (Ik) + Verb (kom) + Preposition (uit) + Noun (Egypte).

• Example 1: Ik kom uit Nederland. (I come from the Netherlands.)  
• Example 2: Hij komt uit Spanje. (He comes from Spain.)  
• Example 3: Zij komt uit Frankrijk. (She comes from France.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Mijn broer komt uit Duitsland. (My brother comes from Germany.)

sentences.nl: Ik ben Lars uit Zweden.
sentences.en: I am Lars from Sweden.

sentences.nl: Wat ga je in Drenthe doen? — Een cursus Nederlands.
sentences.en: What are you going to do in Drenthe? — A Dutch course.

sentences.nl: Echt waar? — Dat is toevallig.
sentences.en: Really? — What a coincidence.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Echt waar? — Dat is toevallig.  
  (Really true? — That is coincidental.)

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Echt waar?" is an expression used to express surprise or disbelief, similar to "Really?" in English.  
• "Dat is toevallig" uses "dat" (that) as a subject pronoun, and "toevallig" (coincidental) as an adjective.  
• Word order is Subject-Verb-Complement, typical for Dutch declarative sentences.

• Examples:  
  - "Echt waar? — Dat had ik niet verwacht." (Really? — I did not expect that.)  
  - "Echt waar? — Dat is ongelooflijk." (Really? — That is unbelievable.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Echt waar? — Dat klinkt interessant." (Really? — That sounds interesting.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, expressing surprise with "Echt waar?" is a common and polite way to engage in conversation when hearing unexpected news.

sentences.nl: Ik ook.
sentences.en: Me too.

sentences.nl: Bij de Dutch Summer School? — Ja, inderdaad.
sentences.en: At the Dutch Summer School? — Yes, indeed.

sentences.nl: Wat leuk.
sentences.en: How nice.

sentences.nl: Dan kunnen we samen reizen tot de eindbestemming.
sentences.en: Then we can travel together to the final destination.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Then can we together travel until the final destination.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Dan" is an adverb meaning "then," used to indicate a sequence in time or a conditional result.  
• "Kunnen" is the modal verb "can" or "be able to," used here in the present tense.  
• "Samen" means "together," indicating joint action.  
• "Tot" is a preposition meaning "until," used to indicate a limit in time or space.  
• "Eindbestemming" is a compound noun from "eind" (end) and "bestemming" (destination), meaning "final destination."

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Maak je geen zorgen" is an imperative sentence meaning "Don't worry." The verb "maak" is the imperative form of "maken" (to make), and "je" is the reflexive pronoun here.  
• "Geen" is used instead of "niet" to negate nouns, in this case, "zorgen" (worries).  
• The sentence literally means "Make yourself no worries," which is a common Dutch way of expressing "Don't worry."

• Similar structure:  
  - "Maak je klaar voor het feest." (Get ready for the party.)  
  - "Maak je geen illusies." (Don't fool yourself.)
